question: Not shared at the level of population class, and this is the same comparison as C-184. P-20 is the same paper as P-19: the two source extracts are byte-identical (Cai et al., Ecotoxicology and Environmental Safety 2024;285:117111). Both papers detect current MCI from clinical and questionnaire tabular data. But P-343's population is hospitalised type 2 diabetes patients aged 40 or over (MCI by AAN 2018 criteria with MoCA < 26), and P-20's is working-age dust-exposed coal miners (inclusion age >= 18; mean 42.6 normal / 48.8 MCI; MCI by a MoCA <= 26 screen). The predictors are tied to each population and share only age and education.

figures.P-343: Internal tuned SVC 0.74 +/- 0.04 (CV mean and SD; mean +/- 1.96 SD [0.662, 0.818]; Hanley-McNeil at the 623-person split, about 218/405: SE = 0.0218, [0.697, 0.783]). External DECODE 0.80, no interval; n = 161, class split derived from the printed accuracy 0.75, recall 0.89 and precision 0.72 as about 88 MCI/73 NC; Hanley-McNeil Q1 = 0.6667, Q2 = 0.7111, SE = 0.0344, CI [0.733, 0.867] ([0.712, 0.888] even at a 40/121 split).
figures.P-20: Identical to P-19. XGBoost 0.959 training / 0.795 validation / 0.913 separately recruited test; logistic 0.818 / 0.816 / 0.778; no interval printed. Derived Hanley-McNeil: test (50/301) XGBoost 0.913, SE = 0.0280, CI [0.858, 0.968]; validation (about 66/322) XGBoost 0.795, SE = 0.0344, CI [0.728, 0.862]; logistic validation 0.816, CI [0.751, 0.881].

matched_figure_check: As in C-184. No figure is reported in the other's population or with the other's predictors. The recorded pairing (external DECODE 0.80 against the same-mine test set 0.913) differs both ways but pairs unlike tiers. On the matched internal tier, P-343's 0.74 lies inside P-20's XGBoost validation interval [0.728, 0.862], and P-20's 0.795 lies inside P-343's mean +/- 1.96 SD range [0.662, 0.818] but just above the Hanley-McNeil interval [0.697, 0.783]; the logistic figures still differ (0.73 against 0.816). Condition 3 is equivocal; condition 1 decides.
performance_validity: Exclusion does not apply: the compared figures are 0.80 and 0.913, both below 0.97.
reason: This record duplicates C-184, since P-20 and P-19 are one paper, and it gets the same judgment. The recorded AUCs differ beyond uncertainty, but they describe MCI detection in different population classes (hospitalised diabetic adults against working-age dust-exposed coal miners) with different predictors and MCI definitions, so condition 1 fails. The pair should be counted once, with C-184.

quotes.quote: External validation with the DECODE cohort yielded an AUC of 0.80, an F1 score of 0.80, and a recall of 0.89.

This cross-sectional study prospectively enrolled adult inpatients diagnosed with T2DM from the Department of Endocrinology at Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital over the period from January 2016 to December 2023.

XGBoost (training set: AUC=0.959, validation set: AUC=0.795) and Logistic Regression (training set: AUC=0.818, validation set: AUC=0.816) models exhibited superior predictive performance. Results from the test set showed that the AUC of the XGBoost model (AUC=0.913) outperformed the Logistic Regression model (AUC=0.778).
A total score of ≤26 is considered to indicate that there may be mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and a total score of > 26 is defined as a normal population.
The data used in this model comes from a single coal mine. More external data may be needed to improve the model’s generalizability.
